s: Who supervised the construction of the Krishna anicut at Bezwada?
x: The Krishna anicut (1853–54) was proposed by Col. Henry Atlock Lake and supervised by Charles Orr.

s: In which year was the main structure of the Godavari anicut at Dowleswaram completed?
x: Cotton's report came in 1844, sanction in 1846, work began in 1847 and the main structure was finished in April 1852.

s: Which of the following pairs (anicut – place) is correctly matched?
x: Penna anicut was at Nellore (1860); Godavari was at Dowleswaram, Krishna at Bezwada and the K.C. Canal at Sunkesula.

s: Which anicut did Veenam Veeranna help Sir Arthur Cotton to build?
x: Veenam Veeranna, an Andhra official, helped Arthur Cotton build the Godavari anicut at Dowleswaram (1847–52).

s: Which structure later replaced Arthur Cotton's old Godavari anicut at Dowleswaram?
x: The old anicut at Dowleswaram was later replaced by the Sir Arthur Cotton Barrage.

s: What was the principal economic cause associated with the Ganjam famine of 1865–66?
o: The Company stopped collecting revenue in the Northern Circars.
Irrigation expansion caused rice prices to fall after the war.
Ryots shifted from cotton to paddy during the American Civil War.
Ryots shifted from paddy to cotton during the American Civil War, followed by a collapse in cotton prices.
x: During the American Civil War, ryots shifted from paddy to cotton. After the war, cotton prices collapsed and rice became scarce, contributing to the Ganjam famine.

s: By what name is the Guntur famine of 1832-33 known?
x: The Guntur famine of 1832-33 is called Dokkala or Nandana Karuvu.

s: Who fed the people during the Kurnool famine of 1866 and later received a gold medal from Queen Victoria?
x: Budda Vengalareddy of Uyyalawada fed the people and received the medal on 1 January 1877.

s: Of the eleven famines Andhra suffered in the late 19th century, which was the most severe?
x: Andhra suffered eleven famines in the late 19th century, 1865-66 being the most severe.

s: Whose canal project was a notable relief effort during the Great Madras Famine of 1876–78?
x: Missionary John Clough's canal relief project was a notable response to the 1876–78 famine, whose laissez-faire relief worsened it.

s: Which famine of 1876–78 devastated Rayalaseema and coastal Andhra?
x: The Great Famine of 1876–78, under Lord Lytton, hit Madras, Mysore, Hyderabad and Bombay and devastated Rayalaseema and coastal Andhra.

s: By what local name is the Guntur famine of 1832–33 known?
x: The 1832–33 Guntur famine, the most serious South Indian famine, is called Dokkala or Nandana Karuvu.

s: Who formed a relief committee during the 1945 famine in Andhra?
x: K.S. Gupta formed a relief committee in the 1945 famine.

s: How many famines hit Andhra in the late 19th century?
x: Andhra suffered 11 famines in the late 19th century.

s: For which of the following is the Guntur famine of 1832–33 known?
o: Being the most serious famine of South India
Being the first famine to get a famine commission
Leading directly to the Famine Code
x: The Guntur famine (Dokkala Karuvu) of 1832–33 is regarded as the most serious South Indian famine; 'Sea of Calamity' was the Orissa famine.

s: What marked the famine policy of the Company period?
o: a comprehensive famine code and extensive relief
no famine code and minimal relief
suspension of revenue in every famine
transfer of all relief to village councils
x: The Company government never adopted a famine code and gave only minimal relief.

s: Who headed the Famine Commission of 1880 whose report led to the Famine Code of 1883?
x: Strachey's 1880 commission followed the 1876-78 famine and led to the 1883 Famine Code; Campbell was 1866, Lyall 1897-98, MacDonnell 1901.

s: In which year was the Famine Code, based on the report of the Richard Strachey Commission, issued?
x: The Famine Code was issued in 1883 on the basis of the Strachey Commission report (APPSC-G1 2022). 1866 is the Campbell Commission (Orissa famine), 1880 is when the Strachey Commission was appointed, and 1901 is the MacDonnell Commission.

s: Who headed the famine commission appointed in 1866 after the Orissa famine?
x: The Campbell Commission of 1866 followed the Orissa famine; Strachey's came in 1880.

s: Which famine commission was set up in 1901 under Curzon?
x: The MacDonnell Commission came in 1901 under Curzon; Lyall's in 1897–98.

s: Which of the following pairs (Famine Commission – Viceroy) is correctly matched?
x: The Strachey Commission belongs to Lytton's time; Campbell was under John Lawrence, Lyall under Elgin II and MacDonnell under Curzon.

s: Which commission assessed the causes of famine and recommended measures against future famines?
x: The Lyall Commission assessed the causes of famine and recommended measures to prevent or mitigate future famines.

s: What was the principal emphasis of the MacDonnell Commission?
x: The MacDonnell Commission stressed early relief and greater irrigation as measures against famine.

s: Which was the last famine commission of the colonial period (1944)?
x: The Woodhead Commission (1944) was the last; the Campbell Commission (1866) was the first.

s: Under which Viceroy was the Lyall Famine Commission appointed?
x: The Lyall Commission (1898) followed the 1896–97 famine under Elgin II; MacDonnell (1901) came under Curzon.

s: Which was the first famine commission of British India?
x: The Campbell Commission (1866), on the Orissa famine, was the first; Woodhead (1944) was the last.

s: Under which Viceroy was the Woodhead Famine Commission appointed after the Bengal famine of 1943?
x: The Woodhead Commission (1944), the last colonial famine commission, was set up under Lord Wavell.

s: Under which Viceroy was the first Famine Commission (Campbell, 1866) appointed?
x: The Campbell Commission of 1866 on the Orissa famine was appointed under Sir John Lawrence.

s: Under the Famine Code, for whom was gratuitous relief meant?
x: The Code gave relief works for the able-bodied and gratuitous relief for the old and infirm.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Famine Code, 1883:
1. It was framed on the recommendations of the Strachey Commission.
2. It provided relief works for the able-bodied.
3. It provided gratuitous relief for the old and infirm.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The 1883 Code came from the Strachey Commission (1880) and provided relief works for the able-bodied and gratuitous relief for the old and infirm.

s: Under the Famine Code of 1883, for whom were relief works meant?
x: Relief works were for the able-bodied (fit); gratuitous relief was for the old and infirm.

s: The Temple wage during the Madras famine of 1877 consisted approximately of which ration?
o: About 1 pound of grain a day on relief works
About 5 pounds of grain a day on relief works
One rupee a day without grain
A weekly ration of ten pounds of rice
x: The Temple wage provided about 1 pound of grain per day on relief works and was criticised as a starvation wage.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Temple wage:
1. It was fixed by Sir Richard Temple in the 1877 Madras famine.
2. It gave about 1 lb of grain a day on relief works.
3. It was praised as a fair living wage.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Temple fixed about 1 lb of grain a day in the 1877 Madras famine; it was criticised as a starvation wage, not praised.

s: To whom does the idea of public works as famine relief go back?
x: Kautilya already prescribed seeds, food, tax exemption and public works in famine.

s: The nationalist critique rejected the view that colonial famines were caused only by what?
x: Rigid revenue collection and grain exports were key causes; famines were not due to monsoon failure alone.

s: Who among the following linked Indian famines with high land revenue and the drain of wealth?
o: Dadabhai Naoroji and Sir Arthur Cotton
x: Dadabhai Naoroji and R.C. Dutt connected famines with the burden of high land revenue and the drain of wealth.

s: Who is the author of 'Open Letters to Lord Curzon' (1900)?
x: R.C. Dutt's Open Letters to Lord Curzon dates to 1900.

s: In which year did R.C. Dutt's 'Open Letters to Lord Curzon' appear?
x: R.C. Dutt wrote 'Open Letters to Lord Curzon' in 1900.

s:
Consider the following statements about the IPC food-insecurity scale:
1. It has five phases.
2. Phase 2 (Stressed) is more severe than Phase 3 (Crisis).
3. Phase 5 is Catastrophe/Famine.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The IPC scale runs Phase 1 Minimal, 2 Stressed, 3 Crisis, 4 Emergency, 5 Catastrophe/Famine; Stressed is less severe than Crisis, so statement 2 is wrong.

s: In the IPC food-insecurity scale, what is Phase 4?
x: The IPC phases are 1 Minimal, 2 Stressed, 3 Crisis, 4 Emergency and 5 Catastrophe/Famine.

s: How many phases does the IPC food-insecurity scale have?
x: The IPC scale has five phases, from Minimal to Catastrophe/Famine.
